learn.hook: Where is the furry cat hiding? Let us find her!
points: Top means the highest part. Bottom means the lowest part.
Above means higher than something. Below means lower.
Inside means within a box or room. Outside means not in it.
On means touching the top. Under means below it.

example.q: A cat sits in a basket. The basket is under a table. Where is the cat?
steps: The cat is in the basket.
So the cat is inside the basket.
The basket is under the table.
example.answer: Inside the basket, under the table

learn.reallife: Shoes go under the bed. Books go inside the bag. The fan is on top, near the ceiling.

games.title: True or false?
items: A ceiling fan is near the top of a room.
The fan hangs from the ceiling, high up.
Your feet are at the top of your body.
Feet are at the bottom. Your head is at the top.
Milk poured in a glass is inside the glass.
The milk is within the glass.
A bird flying in the sky is under the tree.
A bird high in the sky is above the tree.
Roots of a tree are below the ground.
Roots grow down into the soil.

quiz.q: Riya keeps her laddoos in a box. Where are the laddoos?
quiz.explain: She put them in the box. So they are inside it.

quiz.q: Which part of a tree is at the top?
quiz.explain: Leaves are high up on the tree. Roots are at the bottom.

quiz.q: Arjun's cat sleeps under his bed. Is the cat above or below the bed?
quiz.explain: Under means below. So the cat is below the bed.

quiz.q: A kite flies high over the house. The kite is ___ the house.
quiz.explain: High over the house means above the house.

quiz.q: Meena plays in the garden. Her mummy is in the kitchen. Who is outside the house?
quiz.explain: The garden is outside the house. The kitchen is inside.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a garden is inside the house

quiz.q: Kabir puts his bag on the chair. Where is the bag?
quiz.explain: On means resting on the top. So the bag is on top of the chair.

teach.ask: Gappu: I lost my ball! How do I tell where it is?
teach.praise: Yay! Now I can say on, under, inside or outside!
teach.nudge: Can I use words like inside, outside, top or bottom?

learn.hook: Is the ice cream cart near or far? Let us look!
points: Near means close to you. Far means a long way away.
Something near looks big. Something far looks small.
You have a left hand and a right hand.
In a row, we read from left to right.

example.q: In the row 🍎 🍌 🍇, which fruit is in the middle? Which is on the left?
steps: Start from the left: 🍎 is first.
🍌 is next. It is in the middle.
example.answer: 🍌 is in the middle. 🍎 is on the left.

learn.reallife: We look left and right before we cross a road. The moon is far. Your bag is near.

games.title: Near or far?
items: A plane high in the sky

items.text: In 🐶 🐱 🐭, the ___ is in the middle.
In 🚗 🚌 🚲, the ___ is on the far right.
The sun looks small because it is very ___.

quiz.q: Aisha stands next to her school bag. The bus stop is a long walk away. What is near Aisha?
quiz.explain: Next to her means close. So the bag is near.

quiz.q: Which one is far from us?
quiz.explain: The sun is very, very far away. That is why it looks small.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the sun is near because it is bright

quiz.q: In the row ⭐ 🌙 ☀️, what is on the far left?
quiz.explain: Start at the left end of the row. ⭐ comes first.

quiz.q: In the row 🥭 🍌 🍎 🍇, what is just right of 🍌?
quiz.explain: Find 🍌. Move one step right. You reach 🍎.

quiz.q: Harpreet sees two trains. One looks big. One looks tiny. Which train is far?
quiz.explain: Far things look smaller. So the tiny-looking train is far.

quiz.q: Five children stand in a line: Riya, Joseph, Meena, Kabir, Aisha. Who is in the middle?
quiz.explain: Two children are on each side of Meena. So Meena is in the middle.
quiz.mistake: Picks the second or fourth child

teach.ask: Gappu: My friend says the tree is far. What does far mean?
teach.praise: Super! Near is close. Far is a long way. Left and right help too!
teach.nudge: Can you tell me what near and far mean? What about left and right?

chapters.title: What is Long? What is Round?

learn.hook: A snake and a worm went for a walk. Who is longer?
points: Long things stretch a big way from end to end.
Short things stretch only a little way.
To compare, put both ends at the same start line.
Longest means more long than all others. Shortest means less long than all.

example.q: Riya has a pencil and a crayon. Both start at the same line. The pencil ends farther. Which is longer?
steps: Line up one end of both.

learn.reallife: A train is long. A toffee is short. A plait can be long or short.

games.title: Shortest to longest
games.prompt: Put them from shortest to longest

games.title: True or false?
items: A train is longer than a car.
A train has many coaches. It is very long.
A spoon is longer than a bed.
A bed is much longer than a spoon.
To compare length, start both things at the same line.
Then the one that ends farther is longer.
An eraser is longer than a cricket bat.
A cricket bat is much longer.
A giraffe's neck is longer than a cat's tail.
A giraffe has a very long neck.

quiz.q: Which is longer?
quiz.explain: A cricket bat is much longer than a tiny matchstick.

quiz.q: Which is the shortest?
quiz.explain: A paper clip is the shortest of the three.
quiz.mistake: Picks the longest instead of the shortest

quiz.q: Meena's ribbon is long. Aisha's ribbon is short. Whose ribbon is longer?
quiz.explain: Long is more than short. So Meena's ribbon is longer.

quiz.q: Two sticks start at the same line. Stick A ends first. Which is shorter?
quiz.explain: The stick that ends first does not go as far. So Stick A is shorter.

quiz.q: Which animal has a long trunk?
quiz.explain: Only the elephant has a trunk. It is long!
quiz.mistake: Does not know which animal has a trunk

quiz.q: Kabir lays a pen next to a ruler. The ruler is longer. Which is shorter?
quiz.explain: If the ruler is longer, the pen must be shorter.
quiz.mistake: Gets confused between longer and shorter

teach.ask: Gappu: My worm and my pencil look the same. How do I know which is longer?
teach.praise: Clever! Line them up and see which goes farther!
teach.nudge: Should I put them at the same start? Which word tells me long or short?

learn.hook: A ball and a plate are at a party. Which can bounce away?
points: Round things have curved sides, like a ball.
Flat things have flat faces, like a book.
A ball is round all over. It has no flat face.
Some things have both, like a tin can. Its sides are curved. Its top is flat.

example.q: Is a dice round or flat?
steps: All its faces are flat squares.

learn.reallife: A laddoo and a ball are round. A book and a carrom board are flat.

quiz.q: Which one is round all over?
quiz.explain: A ball is curved everywhere. Books and bricks have flat faces.

quiz.q: Which one has flat faces?
quiz.explain: A dice has 6 flat faces. Oranges and marbles are round.

quiz.q: A square gift box is shaped like a ___.
quiz.explain: A box with square faces is like a cube.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every solid is a sphere

quiz.q: A sheet of paper is flat. Which is also flat?
quiz.explain: A notebook cover is flat like the paper. A laddoo and a ball are round.

quiz.q: A tin of ghee has curved sides. What shape is it like?
quiz.explain: A tin has a curved side and two flat round ends. That is a cylinder.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all curved things are spheres

quiz.q: Joseph's birthday cap is pointy at the top. It is like a ___.
quiz.explain: A birthday cap has a round bottom and a point on top. That is a cone.

teach.ask: Gappu: I found a ball and a book. Are they the same shape?
teach.praise: Yes! A ball is round. A book is flat!
teach.nudge: Which one is round? Which one is flat?

learn.hook: Push a ball and push a book. What happens?
points: Round things can roll, like a ball or a bangle.
Things with flat faces slide when we push them.
A cylinder can roll on its side. It slides on its flat end.
A cube cannot roll. It can only slide.

example.q: Can a tin of biscuits roll and slide?
steps: Lay the tin on its curved side. Push. It rolls.
Stand it on its flat end. Push. It slides.
example.answer: Yes, it can roll and slide.

learn.reallife: Wheels roll on the road. A cupboard slides when we push it.

games.title: True or false?
items: A ball is round all over. It rolls easily.
A book can roll down a slope.
A book has flat faces. It slides.
A tin can roll on its curved side.
The curved side lets it roll.
A dice rolls smoothly like a ball.
A dice has flat faces. It tumbles but does not roll smoothly.
A cylinder can slide on its flat end.
Its flat end sits flat, so it can slide.

quiz.q: Which one rolls?
quiz.explain: A marble is round. Round things roll.

quiz.q: Which one will slide, not roll?
quiz.explain: A box has flat faces. It slides.

quiz.q: Why can a bicycle wheel roll?
quiz.explain: Round things roll. A wheel is round.

quiz.q: Arjun pushes a cube. What does it do?
quiz.explain: A cube has flat faces. It slides.

quiz.q: Which can roll on one side and slide on another?
quiz.explain: A tin rolls on its curved side. It slides on its flat end.
quiz.mistake: Picks something that does only one

quiz.q: Aisha wants a toy that rolls down a slide. Which should she pick?
quiz.explain: A ball is round, so it rolls down.

teach.ask: Gappu: Why does my ball roll away but my book stays?
teach.praise: Now I know! Round things roll. Flat things slide!
teach.nudge: What shape is the ball? What does a flat thing do?

learn.hook: Nani brought a basket of mangoes! Let us count them.
points: Each number is one more than the number before it.
The last number we say tells how many.
We can write numbers as digits: 1, 2, 3.

example.q: What number comes just after 6?

learn.reallife: We count steps on stairs, buttons on a shirt, and candles on a cake.

games.title: Count up
games.prompt: Put the numbers in counting order

quiz.q: What comes just after 4?
quiz.explain: Count 1, 2, 3, 4. Next is 5.
quiz.mistake: Says the number before instead of after

quiz.q: What comes just before 9?
quiz.explain: Count 7, 8, 9. Just before 9 is 8.
quiz.mistake: Says the number after instead of before

quiz.q: Which number is between 6 and 8?
quiz.explain: 6, 7, 8. The number in between is 7.
quiz.mistake: Picks a number outside the two

quiz.q: How do we write 'three' as a number?
quiz.explain: Three is written as 3.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the shapes of 3 and 8

quiz.q: Count: 2, 3, 4, ___, 6. What is missing?
quiz.explain: After 4 comes 5. Then 6.

quiz.q: There are 9 steps. Riya has climbed 8. How many more steps to the top?
quiz.explain: From 8, one more step makes 9.
quiz.mistake: Counts the step she is on again

teach.ask: Gappu: I can say 1, 2, 3. What comes next? Why?
teach.praise: Hooray! Each number is one more than before!
teach.nudge: What do we get when we add one more?

learn.hook: Kabir has a plate of laddoos. How many can he share?
points: Touch each thing once and say a number.
Do not skip any. Do not count any twice.
The last number you say is how many in all.
Zero (0) means none at all.

example.q: Count: 🪔 🪔 🪔 🪔 🪔 🪔. How many diyas?

learn.reallife: We count rotis at dinner, kids in a team and diyas at Diwali.

quiz.q: How many mangoes? 🥭🥭🥭🥭🥭
quiz.explain: Touch and count: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

quiz.q: How many diyas? 🪔🪔🪔🪔🪔🪔🪔
quiz.explain: Count each diya once: 1 to 7.

quiz.q: Arjun has no balloons. How many balloons does he have?
quiz.explain: No balloons means zero. We write 0.

quiz.q: How many stars? ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
Meena counts 1, 2, 3, 4 laddoos. How many laddoos are there?
quiz.explain: The last number she said is 4. So there are 4.
quiz.mistake: Gives the first number said, not the last

quiz.q: How many footballs? 🏏 ⚽ ⚽ ⚽
quiz.explain: 🏏 is a bat, not a ball. Count only the footballs: 3.
quiz.mistake: Counts the bat as a ball too

teach.ask: Gappu: I counted my grapes and got a new answer each time! Help!
teach.praise: Touch each one once. The last number is the answer. Got it!
teach.nudge: How many times should I count each grape? Which number is the answer?

learn.hook: Riya has 5 mangoes. Arjun has 3. Who has more?
points: More means a bigger number of things.
Less (or fewer) means a smaller number.
Match them one to one. The side with extras has more.
When both match fully, they are the same (equal).

example.q: Riya has 5 mangoes. Arjun has 3. Who has more? How many more?
steps: Match one of Riya's with one of Arjun's.

learn.reallife: At a party, we check who got more sweets! We pick the shorter queue at a shop.

games.title: True or false?
items: 9 is more. It comes later when we count.

quiz.q: Which is more?
quiz.explain: 9 comes after 6 when we count. So 9 is more.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the first number is bigger

quiz.q: Which is the least?
quiz.explain: 2 comes first when we count. It is the smallest.

quiz.q: Aisha has 🍬🍬🍬🍬. Joseph has 🍬🍬. Who has fewer sweets?
quiz.explain: Joseph has 2. Aisha has 4. 2 is less than 4.

quiz.q: Kabir has 5 kites. Harpreet has 3 kites. How many more does Kabir have?
quiz.explain: Match 3 kites each. Kabir has 2 extra.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two numbers instead of comparing

quiz.q: Which is one more than 6?
quiz.explain: One more than 6 is the next number: 7.

quiz.q: Meena has 4 bangles. Riya has 4 bangles. What is true?
quiz.explain: Both have 4. So they have the same number.
quiz.mistake: Thinks one must always have more

teach.ask: Gappu: I have 3 worms. My friend has 5. Who has more? How do you know?
teach.praise: Yes! Match them up. Extras mean more!
teach.nudge: Which word do we use for a bigger number? How can I check?

learn.hook: Ten fingers, ten toes! Ten is a special number.
points: 10 comes just after 9.
Two numbers can join to make 10, like 6 and 4.
Your two hands have 10 fingers in all.
10 things make one group of ten.

example.q: Arjun has 7 marbles. How many more does he need to make 10?

learn.reallife: Ten fingers help us count. A packet of 10 pencils is one ten.

quiz.q: How many fingers on two hands?
quiz.explain: 5 on one hand and 5 on the other. 5 and 5 make 10.

quiz.q: 8 laddoos are on a plate. How many more make 10?
quiz.explain: Count on from 8: 9, 10. That is 2 more.
quiz.mistake: Adds 8 and 10, or counts one extra

quiz.q: What comes just after 9?
quiz.explain: After 9 comes 10.

quiz.q: 4 and ___ make 10.
quiz.explain: Count on from 4: 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10. That is 6.

quiz.q: Riya has 5 red bangles and 5 green bangles. How many in all?
quiz.explain: 5 and 5 make 10.
quiz.mistake: Writes the numbers side by side

quiz.q: A box holds 10 pencils. It has 3. How many more fit?
quiz.explain: Count on from 3 to 10: that is 7 more.
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of finding what is missing

teach.ask: Gappu: I have 6 seeds. How do I find how many more make 10?
teach.praise: Count on from 6 to 10. Four more! Yay!
teach.nudge: What number do I stop at? How do I count up?

learn.hook: After 10, the numbers keep going! Let us count to 20.
points: Each number is one more than the one before.
20 is two groups of ten.

example.q: What number comes between 14 and 16?

learn.reallife: Bus numbers, page numbers and house numbers use these numbers.

quiz.q: What comes just after 17?
quiz.explain: 17, then 18.

quiz.q: What comes just before 20?
quiz.explain: 18, 19, 20. Just before 20 is 19.

quiz.q: Which number is between 12 and 14?
quiz.explain: 12, 13, 14. 13 is in between.
quiz.mistake: Picks a number outside the two

quiz.q: Which is bigger, 18 or 15?
quiz.explain: 18 comes after 15 when counting. So 18 is bigger.

quiz.q: Count: 15, 16, ___, 18. What is missing?
quiz.explain: After 16 comes 17.

quiz.q: How do we write 'twelve'?
quiz.explain: Twelve is 1 ten and 2 ones. We write 12.

teach.ask: Gappu: I can count to 10. What comes after that?
teach.praise: Wow! 11, 12 ... all the way to 20!
teach.nudge: What comes after 10? Does each number go up by one?

learn.hook: Bundle 10 sticks with a rubber band. That is one ten!
points: 10 ones make 1 ten.
13 is 1 ten and 3 ones.
In 16, the 1 shows the ten. The 6 shows the ones.
20 is 2 tens and 0 ones.

example.q: Harpreet has 1 bundle of 10 sticks and 4 loose sticks. How many sticks?

learn.reallife: Bundles of 10 sticks are quick to count. Pencils come in packs of 10. It makes counting fast.

games.title: True or false?
items: A bundle of 10 ones is one ten.

quiz.q: 1 ten and 6 ones make ___.
quiz.explain: 1 ten is 10. 10 and 6 make 16.
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 and 6, or writes the digits backwards

quiz.q: How many ones are in 13?
quiz.explain: 13 is 1 ten and 3 ones.

quiz.q: How many tens are in 20?
quiz.explain: 10 and 10 make 20. That is 2 tens.
quiz.mistake: Reads the 0 or gives the whole number

quiz.q: Kabir has 10 laddoos in a box and 5 loose. How many laddoos?
quiz.explain: 10 and 5 make 15.

quiz.q: Which number has 1 ten and 9 ones?
quiz.explain: 1 ten is 10. 10 and 9 make 19.

quiz.q: Meena has 17 beads. She makes a group of 10. How many beads are left over?
quiz.explain: 17 is 1 ten and 7 ones. 7 beads are left over.
quiz.mistake: Gives the tens digit instead of ones

teach.ask: Gappu: I have 15 sticks. How can I show them quickly?
teach.praise: Make a bundle of 10. Keep 5 loose. That is 15!
teach.nudge: Can I make a bundle of ten? What about the extra ones?

learn.hook: Two friends bring sweets to share. How many sweets now?
points: Adding means putting things together.
We use the plus sign + to add.
The equal sign = shows the answer.
Start with the bigger number. Count on the smaller one.

example.q: Riya has 4 laddoos. Mummy gives her 3 more. How many now?

learn.reallife: We add when friends join a game or more sweets come to the plate.

quiz.q: 🍎🍎🍎 and 🍎🍎. How many apples in all?
quiz.explain: 3 and 2 make 5. Count all: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.
quiz.mistake: Counts one group only, or one extra

quiz.q: What is 4 + 4?
quiz.explain: Start at 4. Count on 4: 5, 6, 7, 8.
quiz.mistake: Writes the two numbers side by side

quiz.q: Arjun has 5 marbles. He finds 2 more. How many now?
quiz.explain: Start at 5. Count on 2: 6, 7.

quiz.q: 6 children play cricket. 3 more join. How many play now?
quiz.explain: Start at 6. Count on 3: 7, 8, 9.

quiz.q: What is 7 + 0?
quiz.explain: Adding 0 adds nothing. So it stays 7.

quiz.q: Meena has 2 red balloons and 6 blue ones. How many balloons?
quiz.explain: Start at 6. Count on 2: 7, 8.

teach.ask: Gappu: I have 3 berries. I find 2 more. How do I know how many I have?
teach.praise: Put them together and count on. 5 berries! Yum!
teach.nudge: Do I add or take away? How do I count them?

learn.hook: Five birds sit on a wire. Two fly away. How many stay?
points: Subtracting means taking away.
We use the minus sign - to take away.
Count back to find what is left.
Taking away 0 leaves the same number.

example.q: Kabir has 8 grapes. He eats 3. How many are left?

learn.reallife: When we eat sweets, the plate has fewer. When friends leave, fewer play.

games.title: True or false?
items: Take away all 5. None are left.

quiz.q: 5 birds sit on a wire. 2 fly away. How many stay?
quiz.explain: Count back 2 from 5: 4, 3. 3 birds stay.

quiz.q: What is 9 - 3?
quiz.explain: Count back 3 from 9: 8, 7, 6.

quiz.q: Aisha has 7 balloons. 4 pop. How many are left?
quiz.explain: Count back 4 from 7: 6, 5, 4, 3.

quiz.q: Joseph has 6 rotis. He eats all 6. How many are left?
quiz.explain: All are eaten. None are left. 6 - 6 = 0.

quiz.q: What is 8 - 0?
quiz.explain: Taking away nothing leaves 8.

quiz.q: Harpreet has 9 stickers. She gives 5 to Riya. How many does she keep?
quiz.explain: Count back 5 from 9: 8, 7, 6, 5, 4.

teach.ask: Gappu: I had 6 worms. I ate 2. How many are left? How do you know?
teach.praise: Count back from 6: 5, 4. Four left! Thank you!
teach.nudge: Do I take away or add? How do I count back?

learn.hook: Is it a plus story or a minus story? Let us find out!
points: More coming? Then add with +.
Some going away? Then take away with -.
Adding makes the number bigger (but adding 0 keeps it the same).
Taking away makes the number smaller (but taking away 0 keeps it the same).

example.q: There are 4 cows. 3 more cows come. Add or take away?

learn.reallife: Guests arriving means add. Sweets eaten means take away.

quiz.q: 4 ducks swim. 2 more come. Add or take away?
quiz.explain: More ducks come. So we add.
quiz.mistake: Takes away when more are coming

quiz.q: 4 ducks swim. 2 more come. How many ducks now?
8 crayons are in a box. 3 fall out. How many are in the box?
quiz.explain: Some go away, so take away. 8 - 3 = 5.

quiz.q: Which is bigger: 5 + 2 or 5 - 2?
quiz.mistake: Thinks plus and minus give the same answer

quiz.q: 3 + ___ = 8. What is missing?
quiz.explain: Count on from 3 to 8: 4, 5, 6, 7, 8. That is 5.

quiz.q: Riya has 9 diyas. 4 blow out. How many still glow?
quiz.explain: Some go out, so take away. 9 - 4 = 5.

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I know if a story needs plus or minus?
teach.praise: More coming means add. Going away means take away. Smart!
teach.nudge: What do I do when more come? What about when some go away?

learn.hook: The farm has lots of vegetables! Let us add them up.
points: Start with the bigger number. Count on the smaller one.
Make 10 first. Then add what is left.
9 + 4: give 1 to 9 to make 10. Then 10 + 3 = 13.
Changing the order gives the same sum. 3 + 8 = 8 + 3.

example.q: Meena picks 8 carrots and 5 more. How many carrots?

learn.reallife: We add runs in cricket and coins in a piggy bank.

quiz.q: What is 9 + 4?
quiz.explain: Make 10: 9 + 1 = 10. Then add the 3 left: 13.
quiz.mistake: Loses or adds one while counting on

quiz.q: What is 10 + 6?
quiz.explain: 1 ten and 6 ones make 16.

quiz.q: Arjun has 7 tomatoes. He picks 7 more. How many now?
quiz.explain: 7 + 3 = 10. Then 4 more: 14.
quiz.mistake: Counts one too many or too few

quiz.q: Which is the same as 5 + 8?
quiz.explain: Changing the order does not change the sum. Both are 13.

quiz.q: What is 6 + 9?
Kabir has 11 peas. He finds 8 more. How many peas?
quiz.explain: Start at 11. Count on 8: up to 19.

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I add 8 and 5 quickly?
teach.praise: Make 10 first, then add 3. It is 13!
teach.nudge: Can I make a ten first? How many are left to add?

learn.hook: Rabbits nibbled some carrots! How many are left?
points: Count back to take away.
Or count up from the small number to the big one.
15 - 5 = 10. Take away the ones to reach 10.
Taking away makes the number smaller (unless we take away 0).

example.q: There are 14 cabbages. 6 are sold. How many are left?

learn.reallife: When sweets get eaten or toys get given away, we subtract.

games.title: Smallest to biggest answer
games.prompt: Order by the answer, smallest first

quiz.q: What is 15 - 5?
quiz.explain: Take away the 5 ones from 15. 10 is left.

quiz.q: What is 12 - 3?
quiz.explain: Take 2 to reach 10. Take 1 more: 9.

quiz.q: 17 brinjals grow. Riya picks 7. How many are still growing?
quiz.explain: 17 take away 7 is 10.

quiz.q: What is 20 - 8?
quiz.explain: Count up from 8 to 10 is 2. Then 10 more to 20. 2 + 10 = 12.

quiz.q: What is 14 - 9?
quiz.explain: Count up from 9: 10, 11, 12, 13, 14. That is 5.

quiz.q: Aisha has 16 beans. She plants 8. How many are left?

teach.ask: Gappu: I had 13 seeds. I ate 4. How do I find what is left?
teach.praise: Take 3 to reach 10, then 1 more. 9 seeds left!
teach.nudge: Do I count back? Can I stop at 10 on the way?

learn.hook: Every farm has a story. Let us solve them!
points: Read the story slowly.
Find the numbers.
Words like 'more come', 'in all', 'altogether' usually mean add.
Words like 'left', 'gave away', 'ate' usually mean take away.

example.q: Harpreet has 9 potatoes. Her dadi gives her 6 more. How many in all?
steps: 'More' and 'in all' tell us to add.

learn.reallife: At the sabzi market we count what we buy and what is left.

games.title: True or false?
items: In all asks for the total.
'How many are left' usually means we add.
Left means some went away. We take away.
10 hens and 5 more hens make 15 hens.

quiz.q: A farmer has 12 hens. 5 more come. How many hens in all?
quiz.explain: More come, so add. 12 + 5 = 17.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts when the story says more

quiz.q: There are 18 mangoes. A monkey takes 6. How many are left?
quiz.explain: Taken away, so subtract. 18 - 6 = 12.
quiz.mistake: Adds when the story says taken

quiz.q: Joseph plants 8 seeds on Monday and 9 on Tuesday. How many seeds altogether?
quiz.explain: Altogether means add. 8 + 9 = 17.
quiz.mistake: Makes a counting slip when adding

quiz.q: Meena has 15 cucumbers. She sells 9. How many are left?
quiz.explain: Sells means they go away. 15 - 9 = 6.

quiz.q: A cart has 10 pumpkins. 10 more are loaded. How many now?
quiz.explain: Loaded means more. 10 + 10 = 20.

quiz.q: Riya had 13 peas. A bird ate some. Now she has 8. How many did the bird eat?
quiz.explain: Count up from 8 to 13: that is 5.

teach.ask: Gappu: The story says 'how many are left'. Do I add?
teach.praise: Left means take away. In all means add. You are a star!
teach.nudge: Which words tell me to add? Which words tell me to take away?

learn.hook: Lina's family stands in a row for a photo. Who is the tallest?
points: Tall means high from feet to head.
Taller means more tall than another.
Tallest means more tall than everyone else.
Shortest means less tall than everyone else.
Stand on the same floor to compare heights.

example.q: Papa is taller than Lina. Lina is taller than baby Tinu. Who is the tallest?
steps: So Papa is taller than both.

learn.reallife: We line up by height in the school assembly. A coconut tree is taller than a rose plant.

games.title: Shortest to tallest
games.prompt: Put them from shortest to tallest

games.title: True or false?
items: A giraffe is taller than a goat.
A giraffe has very long legs and neck.
A baby is usually taller than her dadi.
A grown-up dadi is taller than a baby.
To compare heights, both should stand on the same floor.
A coconut tree is shorter than a tulsi plant.
A coconut tree is much taller.
If Riya is taller than Meena, Meena is shorter than Riya.

quiz.q: Who is taller?
quiz.explain: A grown-up is taller than a small baby.

quiz.q: Which is the tallest?
quiz.explain: A coconut tree grows very high. It is the tallest.

quiz.q: Arjun is taller than Kabir. Who is shorter?
quiz.explain: If Arjun is taller, Kabir must be shorter.
quiz.mistake: Thinks taller and shorter mean the same

quiz.q: Riya is taller than Aisha. Aisha is taller than Joseph. Who is the shortest?
quiz.explain: Riya is taller than Aisha. Aisha is taller than Joseph. So Joseph is the shortest.

quiz.q: Meena stands on a chair. Harpreet stands on the floor. Is it fair to compare their heights?
quiz.explain: No. Both must stand on the same floor to compare fairly.
quiz.mistake: Forgets both must start at the same level

quiz.q: Which is taller?
quiz.explain: A bus is much taller than a bicycle.

teach.ask: Gappu: My friend and I want to know who is taller. What should we do?
teach.praise: Stand back to back on the same floor. Then we can see!
teach.nudge: Where should we stand? Which word tells who is higher?

learn.hook: No ruler? No problem! Use your hands and feet.
points: A handspan is from thumb tip to little finger tip, spread wide.
We can measure a table in handspans.
We can measure a room in footsteps.
We can measure a book with paper clips or erasers.
Count how many fit from one end to the other.

example.q: Kabir puts erasers in a line along his pencil box. 6 erasers fit. How long is it?

learn.reallife: Mummy measures cloth with her arm. We count steps from class to the gate.

items.text: Put clips end to end with no ___.
Riya uses her hand. Table A is 5 handspans. Table B is 7. Table B is ___.
A handspan is measured with your ___.

quiz.q: Riya measures two desks with her hand. The red desk is 4 handspans. The blue desk is 6. Which is longer?
quiz.explain: 6 of her handspans is more than 4. So the blue desk is longer.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a smaller count means longer

quiz.q: A pencil is 5 paper clips long. How many clips fit along it?
quiz.explain: 5 clips long means 5 clips fit end to end.

quiz.q: Which is best to measure the length of a classroom?
quiz.explain: A classroom is big. Footsteps are quicker for big things.
quiz.mistake: Picks a tiny unit for a big thing

quiz.q: Meena measures her book with blocks: 🟦🟦🟦. How many blocks long?
quiz.explain: Count the blocks: 1, 2, 3.

quiz.q: Aisha measures two mats with her hand. The green mat is 8 handspans. The red is 5. How many more is green?
quiz.explain: 8 - 5 = 3. The green mat is 3 handspans longer.

quiz.q: Joseph measures a rope. He leaves big gaps between his clips. Is his answer right?
options: No, there should be no gaps
quiz.explain: Clips must touch end to end. Gaps give a wrong count.

teach.ask: Gappu: I have no ruler. How can I find how long my nest is?
teach.praise: Use handspans end to end and count them. Brilliant!
teach.nudge: What can I use instead of a ruler? Do I count them?

learn.hook: Papa and Lina measure the same mat. They get different answers! Why?
points: Big hands give a smaller count.
Small hands give a bigger count.
Papa's handspan is bigger than Lina's.
To compare, use the same thing to measure.

example.q: Papa measures a table: 5 handspans. Lina measures it: 8 handspans. Why?
steps: Papa's hand is bigger, so fewer fit.
Lina's hand is smaller, so more fit.
example.answer: Lina's hand is smaller, so she counts more.

learn.reallife: Tailors use one measuring tape so everyone gets the same answer.

games.title: True or false?
items: A bigger hand gives a smaller count.
Fewer big hands fit along the same thing.
Papa and Lina will always get the same handspan count.
Using the same clips helps us compare fairly.
A small foot takes fewer steps across a room.
Measuring with one tape gives everyone the same answer.
The tape does not change size.

quiz.q: Dada and Riya measure the same rug with footsteps. Who takes more steps?
quiz.explain: Riya's feet are smaller. More small steps fit.
quiz.mistake: Thinks bigger feet need more steps

quiz.q: Papa's table is 6 of his handspans. Lina gets 9 of her handspans. Who has the bigger hand?
quiz.explain: Fewer handspans fit, so Papa's hand is bigger.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a bigger count means a bigger hand

quiz.q: A rope is 4 pencils long. It is also ___ clips long.
quiz.explain: A clip is smaller than a pencil. More clips fit along the rope.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the count stays the same with any unit

quiz.q: Arjun and Kabir must compare their desks fairly. What should they do?
quiz.explain: Using the same unit makes the comparison fair.
quiz.mistake: Does not see why the unit must be the same

quiz.q: A stick is 3 big erasers long. Harpreet measures it with small erasers. Which count can be right?
quiz.explain: Small erasers are shorter, so more fit. Only 6 is more than 3.
quiz.mistake: Picks a smaller count for a smaller unit

quiz.q: Meena's book is 7 clips long. Aisha's book is 7 clips long, with the same clips. What is true?
quiz.explain: Same clips, same count. So the books are the same length.
quiz.mistake: Thinks two lengths can never be equal

teach.ask: Gappu: My mama and I measured our nest. We got different numbers! Who is wrong?
teach.praise: Nobody was wrong! Bigger hands count less. Use the same thing to be fair.
teach.nudge: Are our hands the same size? What should we both use?

learn.hook: Counting big piles one by one is slow. Count in tens!
points: Each step adds one more ten.
3 tens is 30. 5 tens is 50.
Ten tens make 100!

example.q: Joseph has 4 packets. Each packet has 10 toffees. How many toffees?

learn.reallife: Shops pack biscuits and pencils in tens. ₹10 notes are counted in tens too.

quiz.q: What is 6 tens?
quiz.explain: Count in tens 6 times: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60.

quiz.q: Count in tens: 30, 40, ___, 60. What is missing?
quiz.explain: Each step adds one ten. After 40 comes 50.

quiz.q: Riya has 3 bundles of 10 sticks. How many sticks?
quiz.explain: 10, 20, 30. Three tens make 30.

quiz.q: How many tens make 80?
quiz.mistake: Gives the whole number instead of the tens

quiz.q: What comes after 90 when counting in tens?
quiz.explain: 90 and one more ten make 100.

quiz.q: Kabir has 2 packs of 10 pencils. How many pencils?
quiz.explain: 10, 20. Two tens make 20.

teach.ask: Gappu: I have a big pile of seeds. How can I count them fast?
teach.praise: Make groups of ten and count 10, 20, 30! So quick!
teach.nudge: Can I make groups? How many in each group?

learn.hook: Every big number has a tens part and a ones part!
points: In 34, the 3 means 3 tens. The 4 means 4 ones.
3 tens and 4 ones make 30 + 4 = 34.
The left digit shows tens. The right digit shows ones.
45 and 54 are different numbers!

example.q: Aisha has 5 bundles of ten sticks and 2 loose sticks. What number is this?

learn.reallife: ₹10 notes and ₹1 coins show tens and ones. Three ₹10 notes and five ₹1 coins make ₹35.

quiz.q: What number is 3 tens and 6 ones?
quiz.explain: 3 tens is 30. 30 and 6 make 36.
quiz.mistake: Swaps the tens and the ones

quiz.q: How many tens are in 72?
quiz.explain: In 72, the 7 is the tens digit. So 7 tens.

quiz.q: How many ones are in 49?
quiz.explain: In 49, the 9 is the ones digit.

quiz.q: Meena has ₹10 notes and ₹1 coins. 2 notes and 5 coins. How much?
Which number has 8 tens and 0 ones?
quiz.explain: 8 tens is 80. No ones, so 80.

quiz.q: Harpreet makes 2 tens and 3 ones with sticks. What number?
quiz.explain: 2 tens is 20. 20 and 3 make 23.

teach.ask: Gappu: What does the 2 mean in 25? Is it just two?
teach.praise: The 2 means 2 tens, that is 20! The 5 means 5 ones!
teach.nudge: Is the 2 tens or ones? What about the 5?

learn.hook: Let us explore numbers all the way up to 99!
points: After 29 comes 30. After 39 comes 40.
To find the bigger number, look at the tens first.
If the tens are the same, look at the ones.
99 is the biggest 2-digit number.

example.q: Which is bigger: 47 or 52?

learn.reallife: House numbers, bus numbers and cricket scores go past 20.

quiz.q: What comes just after 39?
quiz.explain: After 9 ones, we get a new ten. 39 then 40.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the tens stay the same

quiz.q: Which is bigger: 64 or 46?
quiz.explain: 64 has 6 tens. 46 has 4 tens. 6 tens is more.
quiz.mistake: Looks at the ones digit first

quiz.q: Which is smaller: 83 or 87?
quiz.explain: Tens are the same (8). Ones: 3 is less than 7. So 83 is smaller.

quiz.q: What comes just before 60?
quiz.explain: Count back one from 60: 59.

quiz.q: Which number is between 77 and 79?
quiz.explain: 77, 78, 79. 78 is in between.
quiz.mistake: Picks a number outside the two

quiz.q: Arjun scores 58 runs. Kabir scores 85 runs. Who scored more?
quiz.explain: 85 has 8 tens. 58 has 5 tens. 85 is more.

teach.ask: Gappu: Is 38 bigger than 83? They have the same digits!
teach.praise: Look at the tens first! 83 has 8 tens, so it is bigger!
teach.nudge: Which digit should I look at first? Which has more tens?

learn.hook: Utsav time! Rangoli, flags and bead garlands all have patterns.
points: A pattern repeats again and again.
The part that repeats is the 'core'.
🔴🔵🔴🔵 repeats red, blue.
Patterns can use colours, shapes, sizes or sounds.

example.q: Look: 🌼🌸🌼🌸🌼🌸. What part repeats?

learn.reallife: Toran on doors, rangoli at Diwali and stripes on a kurta show patterns.

games.title: True or false?
items: Red, green repeats again and again.
A pattern must use only colours.
Shapes, sizes and sounds can make patterns too.
Clap, stamp, clap, stamp is a pattern.
No part repeats in the same order.

quiz.q: Which is a pattern?
quiz.explain: Red, blue repeats again and again.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any mix of colours is a pattern

quiz.q: What repeats in 🔺⬛🔺⬛🔺⬛?
quiz.explain: A triangle then a square, again and again.

quiz.q: Riya makes a garland: 🌼🌼🌸🌼🌼🌸. What is the core?
quiz.explain: Two yellow flowers then one pink flower repeat.
quiz.mistake: Takes only part of the core

quiz.q: Arjun claps, stamps, claps, stamps. What is this?
quiz.explain: Clap, stamp repeats. That is a pattern.

quiz.q: How many shapes are in the core of ⭐🌙☀️⭐🌙☀️?
quiz.explain: ⭐🌙☀️ repeats. That is 3 shapes.
quiz.mistake: Counts all shapes instead of the core

quiz.q: Which rangoli row is NOT a pattern?
quiz.explain: 🟠🟡🟠🟠🟡🟡 does not repeat the same part again and again.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any colourful row is a pattern

teach.ask: Gappu: What makes a row of beads a pattern?
teach.praise: Yes! The same part repeats again and again!
teach.nudge: Does something happen again and again? What repeats?

learn.hook: Patterns help us guess what comes next!
points: Find the part that repeats.
Say the pattern aloud.
Keep going in the same order.
Check by saying it again from the start.

example.q: What comes next? 🔺🔵🔺🔵🔺 ___

learn.reallife: Lights on a Diwali string blink in patterns. We can guess the next colour!

quiz.q: Look at the beads. What comes next? 🔵🟡🔵🟡🔵 ___
quiz.explain: Blue, yellow repeats. After blue comes yellow.

quiz.q: Look at the sweets. What comes next? 🍬🍬🍫🍬🍬🍫🍬 ___
quiz.explain: Core is 🍬🍬🍫. After one 🍬 comes another 🍬.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the core is only two items

quiz.q: What comes next? clap, clap, jump, clap, clap ___
quiz.explain: Clap, clap, jump repeats. After two claps comes jump.

quiz.q: Meena strings beads: 🔴🟢🔵🔴🟢 ___. What is next?
quiz.explain: Red, green, blue repeats. After green comes blue.
quiz.mistake: Starts the core again too soon

quiz.q: What is missing? 🌸🍃🌸 ___ 🌸🍃
quiz.explain: Flower, leaf repeats. After 🌸 comes 🍃.
quiz.mistake: Repeats the item before the gap

quiz.q: Kabir's flag pattern is 🟧⬜🟩🟧⬜🟩. What are the next two?
quiz.explain: After 🟩 the pattern starts again: 🟧 then ⬜.

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I know what comes next in a pattern?
teach.praise: Find what repeats, then keep going. You did it!
teach.nudge: What part repeats? What comes after the last one?

learn.hook: Numbers can make patterns too!
points: 2, 4, 6, 8 goes up by 2 each time.
5, 10, 15, 20 goes up by 5 each time.
10, 9, 8, 7 goes down by 1 each time.
Find the jump, then keep going.

example.q: What comes next? 3, 6, 9, ___

learn.reallife: House numbers on one side of a road often go 2, 4, 6, 8.

quiz.q: What comes next? 2, 4, 6, 8, ___
quiz.explain: The jump is 2. 8 + 2 = 10.

quiz.q: What comes next? 5, 10, 15, ___
quiz.explain: The jump is 5. 15 + 5 = 20.

quiz.q: What comes next? 10, 9, 8, ___
quiz.explain: It goes down by 1. 8 - 1 = 7.

quiz.q: What is missing? 1, 3, ___, 7, 9
quiz.explain: It goes up by 2. 3 + 2 = 5.

quiz.q: Riya places diyas: 2, 4, 6, 8. How much does each step jump?
quiz.explain: 4 - 2 = 2. Each jump is 2.
quiz.mistake: Counts the steps instead of the jump

quiz.q: What comes next? 20, 30, 40, ___
quiz.explain: The jump is 10. 40 + 10 = 50.

teach.ask: Gappu: Someone said 2, 4, 6, 8. What comes next and why?
teach.praise: Jump by 2 each time. So 10 comes next!
teach.nudge: How much does each number jump? What do I add?

chapters.title: How do I Spend my Day?

learn.hook: The sun rises, the sun sets. Our day has parts!
points: Morning: the sun comes up. We wake up and go to school.
Afternoon: the sun is high. We eat lunch.
Evening: the sun goes down. We play outside.
Night: it is dark. We see the moon and sleep.

example.q: Riya sees the moon and stars. She goes to bed. What part of the day is it?
steps: Moon and stars come out when it is dark.
We sleep when it is dark.

learn.reallife: We say 'Good morning' when we wake up and 'Good night' before sleeping.

games.title: Match the time of day
pairs: Sun sets, play in the park

quiz.q: When do we usually wake up?
quiz.explain: The sun rises in the morning. We wake up then.

quiz.q: When can we see the moon and stars?
quiz.explain: The sky is dark at night. Then we see stars.
quiz.mistake: Thinks stars shine in the day sky

quiz.q: Arjun eats lunch when the sun is high up. What part of the day is it?
quiz.explain: Lunch time, with the sun high, is the afternoon.

quiz.q: The sun is going down. Birds fly home. When is it?
quiz.explain: The sun sets in the evening.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the sun sets in the morning

quiz.q: Which comes just after morning?
quiz.explain: Morning, then afternoon, then evening, then night.

quiz.q: What do we say before going to sleep?
quiz.explain: We sleep at night, so we say good night.
quiz.mistake: Picks the wrong greeting for the time

teach.ask: Gappu: Why do you say 'Good morning' and 'Good night'?
teach.praise: Morning is when the sun rises. Night is dark, time to sleep!
teach.nudge: When does the sun come up? When is it dark?

learn.hook: Things in a day happen in order. What comes first?
points: First we wake up. Next we brush. Then we eat breakfast.
We use words like first, next, then and last.
Before means earlier. After means later.
Some things must happen before others.

example.q: Put in order: eat breakfast, wake up, go to school.
example.answer: Wake up, eat breakfast, go to school

learn.reallife: Making chai has an order: boil water, add tea leaves, add milk, then pour.

games.title: True or false?
items: We wear shoes before we wear socks.
Socks go on first, then shoes.
We wash hands before we eat.
We dry ourselves after a bath.
First the bath, then we dry off.
We brush our teeth after we wake up.
First we wake up, then we brush.
We eat a mango before we peel it.
We peel or cut it first, then eat.

quiz.q: What do we do first?
quiz.explain: Socks go on first. Then shoes. Then we run!

quiz.q: Kabir plants a seed. What happens next?
quiz.explain: After planting, we water the seed. The tree grows much later.

quiz.q: Meena eats dinner, then brushes her teeth, then sleeps. What does she do last?
quiz.explain: Sleeping is the last thing in her list.

quiz.q: Which happens before lunch?
quiz.explain: Breakfast is in the morning. Lunch comes after it.

quiz.q: Aisha makes a sandwich. What does she do first?
quiz.explain: She needs bread first. She eats later.

quiz.q: Joseph comes home from school. What does he do after that?
quiz.explain: After coming home, he washes up. The others happen in the morning.

teach.ask: Gappu: I wore my shoes and then tried to put on socks. What went wrong?
teach.praise: Socks first, then shoes! Order matters. Thank you!
teach.nudge: What should come first? What comes after?

learn.hook: Some jobs are quick. Some take a long time!
points: Blinking takes a very short time.
Brushing teeth takes a few minutes.
A school day takes many hours.
Growing a mango tree takes years!

example.q: Which takes longer: drinking a glass of water or watching a cricket match?
steps: Drinking water takes a few seconds.
A cricket match takes many hours.

learn.reallife: A train trip to Nani's house takes longer than a walk to the shop.

quiz.q: Which takes less time?
quiz.explain: A sneeze is over in a second. We sleep for many hours.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up less and more time

quiz.q: Which takes the longest?
quiz.explain: A mango tree takes years to grow.

quiz.q: Which takes more time?
quiz.explain: A cricket match lasts many hours. Washing hands is quick.

quiz.q: Riya walks to the park gate. Harpreet walks all around the big park. They walk at the same speed. Who takes longer?
quiz.explain: Harpreet walks much farther. A longer walk takes more time.

quiz.q: Which can you do in one clap's time?
quiz.explain: A blink is as quick as a clap.
quiz.mistake: Does not know which jobs are quick

quiz.q: Which takes longer?
quiz.explain: Making rangoli takes a long time. Opening a door is quick.

teach.ask: Gappu: Does eating a laddoo take longer than growing a tree?
teach.praise: Ha! Eating is quick. Growing a tree takes years!
teach.nudge: Which one is quick? Which one takes a long time?

learn.hook: Mummy puts laddoos on plates. Does every plate get the same?
points: Equal groups have the same number in each.
3 plates with 2 laddoos each are equal groups.
Count the groups. Count how many in one group.
Groups that are not the same are unequal.

example.q: 4 plates. Each plate has 2 laddoos. Are the groups equal? How many laddoos?
steps: Each plate has 2. So the groups are equal.

learn.reallife: Pairs of socks, wheels on cars and fingers on hands come in equal groups.

games.title: True or false?
items: One group has 1, the other has 2.
A bicycle has 2 wheels. 3 bicycles have 3 groups of 2 wheels.
Each bicycle gives a group of 2.
Equal groups means every group has the same number.

quiz.q: Which shows equal groups?
quiz.explain: Both groups have 3 bananas. They are equal.

quiz.q: 3 boxes have 4 crayons each. How many groups are there?
quiz.explain: Each box is one group. There are 3 boxes.
quiz.mistake: Gives the number in each group

quiz.q: 🐟🐟🐟 | 🐟🐟🐟. How many fish in each group?
quiz.explain: Each group has 3 fish.

quiz.q: 2 cars. Each car has 4 wheels. How many wheels?
quiz.explain: 4 and 4 make 8.

quiz.q: Riya puts 10 grapes into 2 equal bowls. How many in each bowl?
quiz.explain: 5 and 5 make 10. So each bowl has 5.

quiz.q: Arjun has 🍪🍪🍪 | 🍪. How can he make the groups equal?
options: Move 1 cookie to the small group
Add 2 cookies to the big group
quiz.explain: Then each group has 2. 2 and 2 are equal.
quiz.mistake: Does not see how to share evenly

teach.ask: Gappu: I gave my friends 1, 3 and 2 seeds. Is that fair?
teach.praise: Equal groups means each friend gets the same. Now it's fair!
teach.nudge: Does every friend get the same number? What does equal mean?

learn.hook: Add the same number again and again. That is repeated addition!
points: 3 groups of 2 is 2 + 2 + 2.
We can skip count: 2, 4, 6.
4 groups of 5 is 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 20.

example.q: Kabir has 3 packets. Each has 5 toffees. How many toffees?

learn.reallife: A cricket team gets 2 runs, 2 runs, 2 runs. That is repeated addition!

quiz.q: What is 3 + 3 + 3?
quiz.explain: 3, 6, 9. Three 3s make 9.

quiz.q: 4 groups of 2 is the same as ___.
quiz.explain: 4 groups of 2 means add 2 four times.
quiz.mistake: Adds the number of groups and the group size

quiz.q: Meena has 2 plates with 5 idlis each. How many idlis?
Skip count by 2: 2, 4, 6, ___. What comes next?
quiz.explain: Each step adds 2. 6 + 2 = 8.

quiz.q: 5 children each hold 2 balloons. How many balloons?
Harpreet has 3 rows of 4 stickers. How many stickers?

teach.ask: Gappu: I have 3 nests with 2 eggs each. How do I find all the eggs?
teach.praise: 2 + 2 + 2 = 6. I have 6 eggs!
teach.nudge: How many eggs in each nest? Do I add them again and again?

learn.hook: '3 times 2' means 2, three times!
points: 3 times 2 means 3 groups of 2.
3 times 2 is 2 + 2 + 2 = 6.
2 times 5 is 5 + 5 = 10.
'Times' tells how many groups there are.

example.q: Joseph hops 4 times. Each hop is 2 steps. How far does he go?

learn.reallife: We clap 3 times, 2 claps each time. A shopkeeper puts 2 bananas in a bag, 4 times.

quiz.q: What is 3 times 2?
quiz.explain: 3 times 2 is 2 + 2 + 2 = 6.

quiz.q: A frog jumps 3 steps at a time. It jumps 4 times. Where does it land from 0?
Which is the same as 2 times 4?
quiz.explain: 2 times 4 means two 4s: 4 + 4.

quiz.q: Aisha buys 2 packets of 10 pencils. How many pencils?
5 times 1 is ___.
Riya claps 2 times in each round. She does 3 rounds. How many claps?

teach.ask: Gappu: What does '4 times 2' mean? I am confused!
teach.praise: 4 groups of 2! 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8. I get it now!
teach.nudge: How many groups? What do I add again and again?

learn.hook: Let us go to the market! First, let us know our money.
points: Our money is the rupee. We write ₹.
Coins are round and made of metal: ₹1, ₹2, ₹5, ₹10.
Notes are made of paper: ₹10, ₹20, ₹50, ₹100.
A ₹5 coin is worth five ₹1 coins.

example.q: How many ₹1 coins make ₹5?

learn.reallife: We pay with coins and notes at the sabzi market and the sweet shop.

games.title: Smallest to biggest
games.prompt: Put money in order, least first

quiz.q: Which is worth the most?
quiz.explain: 5 is more than 2 and 1. So ₹5 is worth the most.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a bigger-looking coin is worth more

quiz.q: How many ₹1 coins make ₹2?
quiz.mistake: Thinks one coin of any kind is the same

quiz.q: Which one is a note, not a coin?
quiz.explain: ₹100 comes as a paper note. ₹1 and ₹2 are coins.
quiz.mistake: Does not know which money is paper

quiz.q: Riya has two ₹5 coins. How much money is that?
How many ₹10 notes make ₹20?
quiz.explain: ₹10 + ₹10 = ₹20. That is 2 notes.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the value with the number of notes

quiz.q: What sign do we use for rupees?
quiz.explain: ₹ is the sign for our rupee.

teach.ask: Gappu: My shiny coin and a paper note. Which is money?
teach.praise: Both! Coins and notes are both rupees. Wow!
teach.nudge: Are coins money? Are notes money too? What do we call our money?

learn.hook: Arjun has a few coins. How much money does he have?
points: Add the value of each coin or note.
Start with the biggest one. Count on.
Different coins can make the same amount.

example.q: Meena has a ₹10 coin, a ₹5 coin and a ₹2 coin. How much in all?

learn.reallife: We count money in our piggy bank. Shopkeepers count the money we give.

quiz.q: Kabir has ₹10 and ₹2. How much in all?
Aisha has three ₹2 coins. How much money?
quiz.mistake: Counts the coins, not their value

quiz.q: Which makes ₹10?
Harpreet has a ₹10 note, a ₹5 coin and a ₹1 coin. How much?
Joseph has ₹20 and Riya has ₹10. How much together?
Meena has 4 coins: ₹5, ₹5, ₹2, ₹1. How much?
quiz.mistake: Counts the coins instead of adding their values

teach.ask: Gappu: I have 3 coins. So I have ₹3, right?
teach.praise: Oh! Each coin has its own value. I must add them up!
teach.nudge: Is every coin worth ₹1? What should I add?

learn.hook: At the mela, toys have prices. Can we buy them?
points: The price tells how much a thing costs.
If we have enough money, we can buy it.
If we pay more, we get some money back. That is change.
Change = money given - price.

example.q: A balloon costs ₹7. Riya pays ₹10. How much change?

learn.reallife: At the sweet shop, the shopkeeper gives back change when we pay more.

games.title: True or false?
items: With ₹10, Arjun can buy a ₹8 toy.
With ₹5, Meena can buy a ₹9 book.
₹5 is less than ₹9. Not enough money.
Pay ₹10 for a ₹4 ball. Change is ₹6.
Pay ₹20 for a ₹12 cap. Change is ₹12.
If you pay the exact price, you get no change.

quiz.q: A pencil costs ₹5. Kabir pays ₹10. How much change?
quiz.mistake: Adds the price to the money paid

quiz.q: A laddoo costs ₹8. Aisha has ₹6. Can she buy it?
quiz.explain: ₹6 is less than ₹8. She needs ₹2 more.

quiz.q: A toy car costs ₹13. Joseph pays ₹20. How much change?
quiz.explain: Count up from 13 to 20: that is 7.

quiz.q: Riya buys a ₹4 eraser and a ₹5 pencil. How much does she spend?
Riya pays ₹10 for things worth ₹9. How much change?
Arjun has ₹15. Which can he buy?
quiz.explain: ₹12 is less than ₹15. The others cost more than he has.
quiz.mistake: Picks a price higher than his money

teach.ask: Gappu: The kite costs ₹6. I gave ₹10. Why did I get money back?
teach.praise: I paid more than the price, so I get ₹4 change!
teach.nudge: Did I pay more than the price? How do I find the change?

learn.hook: Kabir's toys are all mixed up! Let us sort them.
points: Sorting means putting things that are alike together.
We can sort by colour, shape, size or kind.
Each group shares something the same.
The same toys can be sorted in different ways.

example.q: Sort: 🚗 🧸 🚌 🪁 🚲. Which toys move on wheels?

learn.reallife: We sort clothes in a cupboard, spoons in a drawer and books on a shelf.

quiz.q: Which one does NOT belong? 🍎 🍌 🚗 🍇
quiz.explain: 🍎, 🍌 and 🍇 are fruits. 🚗 is a car.
quiz.mistake: Does not see what the group has in common

quiz.q: Riya sorts by colour. Where does a red ball go?
quiz.explain: She is sorting by colour, so red goes with red.
quiz.mistake: Uses a different rule than the one given

quiz.q: Which is a good way to sort crayons?
quiz.explain: Crayons have different colours. Colour is easy to see.
quiz.mistake: Picks a rule that does not fit

quiz.q: What is the same in 🔺 🔺 🔺?
quiz.explain: All three are triangles. They have the same shape.
quiz.mistake: Looks at something that is not shown

quiz.q: Which toy does NOT belong? ⚽ 🏀 🎾 🧸
quiz.explain: ⚽, 🏀 and 🎾 are balls. 🧸 is a teddy.
quiz.mistake: Picks an item that fits the group

quiz.q: Arjun puts 🚗 🚌 🚲 together. What rule did he use?
quiz.explain: A car, a bus and a cycle all have wheels.
quiz.mistake: Does not see the common feature

teach.ask: Gappu: My toy box is a mess! How do I sort it?
teach.praise: Put the same kind together. Now my box is neat!
teach.nudge: What should go together? By colour or by kind?

learn.hook: After sorting, we can count each group!
points: Sort the things first.
Count each group.
Then we can see which group has the most.
We can also find how many in all.

example.q: 🚗🚗🚗 🧸🧸 ⚽⚽⚽⚽. Which group has the most?

learn.reallife: A teacher counts how many children bring tiffin and how many buy lunch.

quiz.q: 🍎🍎🍎🍎🍌🍌. How many apples?
quiz.explain: Count only the apples: 1, 2, 3, 4.

quiz.q: 🧸🧸🚗🚗🚗🚗🚗. Are there more teddies or cars?
quiz.explain: Cars: 5. Teddies: 2. 5 is more.

quiz.q: ⚽⚽⚽ 🏀🏀. How many balls in all?
Meena has 6 dolls and 4 blocks. How many more dolls than blocks?
🎈🎈🎈 🪁🪁🪁. What is true?
quiz.explain: 3 balloons and 3 kites. They are the same.
quiz.mistake: Thinks one group must be bigger

quiz.q: 🐶🐶 🐱🐱🐱 🐰. Which group has the fewest?
quiz.explain: Dogs: 2. Cats: 3. Rabbit: 1. 1 is the fewest.
quiz.mistake: Picks the most instead of the fewest

teach.ask: Gappu: There are cars and teddies all mixed up. Which is more?
teach.praise: Sort them, count each group, then compare. Easy!
teach.nudge: Should I sort them first? Then what do I do?

learn.hook: A picture graph shows counts with little pictures!
points: Each picture stands for one thing.
A row with more pictures means more things.
We count the pictures in each row.
We can see the most and the least quickly.

example.q: Toys in class: Cars 🚗🚗🚗🚗, Balls ⚽⚽, Dolls 🪆🪆🪆. Which toy is the most?

learn.reallife: Teachers make picture graphs of favourite fruits or how children come to school.

games.title: Read the graph: 🍎🍎🍎 apples, 🍌🍌🍌🍌🍌 bananas, 🥭🥭 mangoes
items: Only 2 mangoes. That is the least.
There are more apples than bananas.

games.title: Fill from the graph: 🚌 🚌 🚌 bus, 🚲 🚲 cycle, 🚶 🚶 🚶 🚶 walk

quiz.q: Favourite sweets: Laddoo 🟡🟡🟡🟡, Jalebi 🟠🟠, Barfi ⚪⚪⚪. Which is liked most?
quiz.explain: Laddoo has 4 pictures. That is the most.

quiz.q: Pets: Dogs 🐶🐶🐶, Cats 🐱🐱, Fish 🐟🐟🐟🐟🐟. How many fish?
quiz.explain: Count the fish row: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

quiz.q: Pets: Dogs 🐶🐶🐶, Cats 🐱🐱, Fish 🐟🐟🐟🐟🐟. Which pet is the least?
quiz.explain: Cats have only 2 pictures. That is the least.

quiz.q: Kites: Riya 🪁🪁🪁, Arjun 🪁🪁🪁🪁🪁🪁. How many more does Arjun have?
Fruits: 🍎🍎 apples, 🍌🍌🍌 bananas, 🍇🍇🍇🍇 grapes. How many fruits in all?
In a picture graph, what does one 🌸 show?
quiz.explain: In our graphs, each picture stands for one thing.

teach.ask: Gappu: What is a picture graph? How do I read it?
teach.praise: Count the pictures in each row. The longest row has the most!
teach.nudge: What does each picture show? How do I find the most?
